title: This Frog Freezes Solid Every Winter, and Its Heart Stops
subject: wood frog

scenes.text: Every winter this frog freezes solid and comes back to life.
Up to 65 percent of its body water turns to ice. Its heart stops. It stops breathing.
Ice normally shreds cells. So how does it survive?
Its liver floods the body with glucose, a natural antifreeze that protects the cells.
The ice stays outside the cells, in the gaps between them.
When spring warms the soil, the heart starts beating again. A frog that dies every winter.

description:
The wood frog lets up to 65 percent of its body water freeze each winter.
Its heart stops, then restarts when it thaws, thanks to glucose antifreeze.
Could you survive being frozen?
first_comment: It does this every winter across northern North America. What's the toughest survivor you know of?
